headline: PEACE TALKS DRAG GOLD TO $4,583 AS HORMUZ TANKER ATTACK CAPS THE SELLOFF
snippet: Gold fell 0.63% to $4,583/oz Monday as investors weighed signs of US-Iran peace talk progress against a fresh tanker strike in the Strait of Hormuz following President Trump's plan to escort vessels through the waterway. The metal remains down roughly 13% since the Middle East conflict entered its tenth week, though central bank buying has provided a floor.

headline: SILVER HITS $75.7, OUTPACES GOLD AS BIG TECH'S $715B AI CAPEX VALIDATES INDUSTRIAL DEMAND THESIS
snippet: Silver surged ~1% Monday to $75.7/oz, outperforming gold as fresh hyperscaler earnings confirmed $715B in AI infrastructure spending from Meta, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon — nearly double last year's $375B. China's March silver imports hit an all-time high of 836 tonnes driven by solar manufacturing and retail investor demand.

headline: CHINA'S SULFURIC ACID BAN NOW IN FORCE — CHILE'S 1-MILLION-TONNE COPPER LIFELINE AT RISK IN H2 2026
snippet: China's halt on sulfuric acid exports — effective May 1 — threatens heap-leach copper refining operations in Chile, which imports over 1 million tonnes of the critical reagent annually. The ban compounds disruptions from Middle East conflict-driven sulphur shortages, with analysts warning Chile's copper output faces a supply squeeze in H2 2026.

headline: JUNIOR MINERS WINNING THE 2026 EXPLORATION RACE AS AFRICA AND CENTRAL ASIA HEAT UP
snippet: A May 4 analysis identifies the Kalahari Copper Belt, West African gold belts, and Central Asian greenstone terranes as the hottest junior exploration frontiers heading into mid-2026. Australian-listed Cobre Limited is highlighted as proof of concept for the junior-to-major pipeline in Botswana, drawing capital to the region.

headline: NOAA DECLARES TMC SEABED MINING APPLICATION IN FULL COMPLIANCE — PACIFIC BATTERY METALS ONE STEP FROM COMMERCIAL PERMIT
snippet: NOAA ruled The Metals Company's deep-seabed mining application in full compliance on May 1, advancing a 619-million-tonne polymetallic nodule resource in the Clarion Clipperton Zone toward a final commercial recovery permit expected in Q1 2027. The project would supply nickel, cobalt, manganese, and copper for the battery supply chain at scale.

headline: COT REPORT MAY 1: SPECULATIVE GOLD LONGS TRIMMED, COMMERCIAL SHORTS EASE — MARKET AWAITS ITS NEXT CATALYST
snippet: The latest CFTC Commitment of Traders data shows speculative gold longs pulling back from elevated levels while commercial short positions have also eased, pointing to a neutral near-term setup. Silver positioning and USD sentiment offer mixed signals ahead of April services PMI, jobless claims, and University of Michigan inflation expectations data due this week.

headline: CHINA FORMALIZES RARE EARTH CRACKDOWN: FINES UP TO 5X ILLEGAL GAINS, LICENSE REVOCATION ON THE TABLE
snippet: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology issued draft enforcement rules covering the full rare earth supply chain — from mining through separation and processing — with penalties up to five times illegal gains and potential license revocation. The measures deepen Beijing's institutional grip just as Western consolidation and capital formation accelerate to challenge Chinese dominance.

headline: HONEY BADGER SILVER (TUF.V) ROCKETS 63% IN ONE WEEK, LEADS TSXV PRECIOUS METALS GAINERS
snippet: Honey Badger Silver Inc. (TSXV: TUF) topped Canadian junior mining gainers with a 63% weekly surge as of May 1, 2026, as speculative interest in silver exploration stories intensifies alongside the metal's push toward $76/oz. The move headlined a strong week for TSX-V precious metals names.

headline: GOLD, SILVER AND COPPER: WHY BARRICK AND NEWMONT BELONG IN EVERY PORTFOLIO AHEAD OF THE COMMODITY RALLY
snippet: A May 1 Stockhouse contributor piece argues that gold, silver, platinum, and copper are entering a synchronized rally phase driven by structural supply deficits, central bank accumulation, and AI-led industrial consumption. Barrick, Newmont, and Power Metallic Mines are named as best-positioned majors to capture the move.

headline: K92 MINING REITERATES 2026 GUIDANCE; GOLD MINERS STILL TRADE AT 9.6X CASH FLOW DESPITE RECORD MARGINS
snippet: K92 Mining (TSX: KNT) reaffirmed its 2026 production guidance at Kainantu in PNG and holds technical support above its 50-day moving average, per the latest GoldSeek SWOT analysis. Senior gold producers as a group still trade at just 9.6x forward cash flow — near the five-year average — despite generating record margins at $4,500+ gold, suggesting significant re-rating potential.
